# partiteai_access_point (Resource)

An access point: a way into meshes for callers who sign in with a token from a trusted issuer rather than an API key.



<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Resource name

### Optional

- `authorization_server_url` (String) Advertised to MCP clients as where to log in
- `boundary_ids` (Set of String) IDs of the boundaries conversations created through the access point are checked against
- `client_token_lifetime_seconds` (Number) How long a token issued to a client lasts, from 300 to 86400 seconds
- `description` (String) Resource description
- `issuers` (Attributes List) The issuers whose tokens the access point accepts (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--issuers))
- `tags` (Attributes List) Tags for the resource (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--tags))

### Read-Only

- `created_at` (String) Timestamp when the resource was created
- `id` (String) Resource identifier
- `updated_at` (String) Timestamp when the resource was last updated
- `url` (String) Where callers reach the access point. Tokens it issues to its clients carry it as their `iss` and `aud`.

<a id="nestedatt--issuers"></a>
### Nested Schema for `issuers`

Required:

- `issuer` (String) The `iss` a token from this issuer carries

Optional:

- `audience` (String) Must be in a token's `aud`. Left out, it is the access point's URL.
- `check_audience` (Boolean) Whether a token's `aud` is checked. Turning it off accepts tokens the issuer made for other services and ID tokens, and skips the audience check MCP clients expect.
- `jwks` (String) A key set, as JSON, for an issuer that publishes none
- `jwks_url` (String) Where the issuer publishes its key set. Set exactly one of `jwks_url` and `jwks`.


<a id="nestedatt--tags"></a>
### Nested Schema for `tags`

Required:

- `name` (String) Tag name
- `value` (String) Tag value
